column1: # Ground truth for mix(), generated from meo-canvas v1's built module
# (`dist/esm/animate/interpolate.js`) rather than from either v2 implementation.
# v1 at tag v9.0.2, commit 890eed2, working tree clean -- the same provenance
# the four original tables name, verified by reproducing all 612 of their rows.
# # The `surface` column, and why a table needs one
# `mix` is generic over what v1 calls `Animatable`, and the two v2 surfaces do
# not implement it over the same set. Rust has exactly two impls, `f64` and
# `Rgba`; JavaScript also mixes arrays element-wise. So `kind = array` rows are
# **JavaScript-only** and carry `surface = js-only`, which a Rust walker skips.
# That is a recorded parity gap rather than a walker convenience: an array is a
# capability one surface ships and the other does not, and the column is where
# it is visible instead of being absent from a Rust table nobody compares.
# `t` runs outside 0..1 because `mix` does not clamp on either v2 surface --
# both diverge from v1's `mixColor` in the same direction, deliberately, since
# the overshooting curves exist to produce exactly that.
# Colour values are quoted for the reason `parse-color.tsv` gives.
# # v1 clamps colour and does not clamp numbers, inside one function
# `mix` delegates its colour case to `mixColor`, which clamps `t`, while its
# number case does not -- so v1 contradicts itself between two arms of the same
# generic. Both v2 surfaces clamp neither, deliberately. The `diverges` rows are
# the colour ones outside 0..1; the number rows outside 0..1 agree.
